evidence: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/components/Toast.tsx:172-189 — ToastItem.handleCopy() schedules `setTimeout(() => setCopied(false), 2000)` on BOTH the success path (:177) and the execCommand fallback path (:187) to reset the 'Copied' button label, but the timer id is neither stored in a ref nor cleared on unmount. ToastItem unmounts whenever its toast auto-dismisses (ToastProvider auto-dismiss via getDefaultDuration — error toasts, which are the ones that render this copy button, default to a finite duration) or is manually dismissed. If the user clicks copy and the toast then unmounts within the 2s window, the pending timer fires setCopied(false) on an unmounted component — a setState-after-unmount leak.

This is an internal-consistency defect: every OTHER timer in the same file and its sibling are tracked and cleaned up — ToastProvider tracks auto-dismiss timers in `timeoutRefs` (Map) and clears them all in a useEffect cleanup (Toast.tsx:97-107, and per-toast in removeToast :109-117), and components/Announcer.tsx:85-93 clears all four of its setTimeout refs on unmount. ToastItem's copy-feedback timer is the lone unmanaged timer.

Severity low: React 18 silently no-ops a setState on an unmounted component (no console warning, no crash, no user-visible breakage), so this is a latent smell rather than an active bug — but it violates the team's own established cleanup pattern and would resurface as a real warning under React 19 strict/concurrent flows or in test teardown. Fix (frontend-only, cloud-landable, no backend/DB): store the timer id in a useRef inside ToastItem and clearTimeout it in a useEffect(() => () => clearTimeout(ref.current), []) cleanup, mirroring ToastProvider/Announcer; or gate the setCopied(false) behind a mounted ref. Add a Vitest case that unmounts ToastItem immediately after a copy click and asserts no act() warning / no state update.
